_meta.title: Forensic Semiotics — Authoritarian Propaganda Trope Taxonomy
_meta.scope: Regime-agnostic: covers Kremlin-aligned propaganda and non-Western authoritarian media (Myanmar, Eritrea, Syria, Cuba, Turkmenistan, Western Sahara/SADR, Yemen, Tajikistan, Eswatini, et al.).

narrative_strategy.description: Four strategic categories of narrative suppression and manipulation
narrative_strategy.source: Lank & Antai — Narrative Strategy and Information Warfare, International Journal of Communication, 2025

ellul_type.description: Ellul's typology of propaganda by intent: agitation = mobilise for action; integration = normalise existing order
ellul_type.source: Jacques Ellul — Propaganda: The Formation of Men's Attitudes (1965)

ellul_axis.description: Ellul's axis: vertical = top-down state messaging; horizontal = peer-group/grassroots diffusion
ellul_axis.source: Jacques Ellul — Propaganda: The Formation of Men's Attitudes (1965)

eco_properties.description: Umberto Eco's 14 features of Ur-Fascism as a proto-fascist content checklist
values: The Cult of Action for Action's Sake
Appeal to a Frustrated Middle Class
Enemies Too Strong and Too Weak
eco_properties.source: Umberto Eco — Ur-Fascism, New York Review of Books, 1995

san_martino_techniques.description: 18 propaganda techniques from fine-grained NLP analysis of news articles
san_martino_techniques.source: Da San Martino et al. — Fine-Grained Analysis of Propaganda in News Articles, ACL 2019

ipa_techniques.description: 7 classic propaganda techniques from the Institute for Propaganda Analysis

eudisinfo_rhetoric.description: EUvsDisinfo Modus Trollerandi — 7 rhetorical devices (SWAMPED acronym)
eudisinfo_rhetoric.source: EUvsDisinfo — Modus Trollerandi: The Kremlin's Rhetoric

eudisinfo_conspiracy.description: Recurring conspiracy theory archetypes in pro-Kremlin disinformation
eudisinfo_conspiracy.source: EUvsDisinfo — Disinformation Cases Database & DISARM Framework

eudisinfo_ttp.description: Tactics, Techniques and Procedures from the DISARM disinformation framework
eudisinfo_ttp.source: DISARM Framework / EUvsDisinfo — Tactics, Techniques & Procedures

myth_function.description: Temporal-functional role of the trope in the political myth system (Flood / Tudor typology)
myth_function.notes: cosmogonic = founding/origin myth; eschatological = final battle / end-times narrative; theodicy = suffering is meaningful / sacrifice justified; heroic = leader as saviour; providential = historical mission / destiny of the nation
myth_function.source: Flood, C. — Political Myth: A Theoretical Introduction (Routledge, 2002); Tudor, H. — Political Myth (Macmillan, 1972)

enemy_type.description: How the enemy is constructed in the trope's narrative (Volkan / Keen typology)
enemy_type.notes: external = foreign state or actor; internal = traitor / fifth column / ethnic minority within; ontological = constitutionally different or inferior by nature; shadow = occult / conspiratorial hidden enemy that is everywhere
enemy_type.source: Volkan, V. — The Need to Have Enemies and Allies (Jason Aronson, 1988); Keen, S. — Faces of the Enemy (Harper & Row, 1986)

legitimation_mode.description: How the propaganda claim achieves authority — one or more modes (van Leeuwen typology)
legitimation_mode.notes: authorization = appeals to authority of person/tradition/law; moral = appeals to shared value systems; rationalization = instrumental/functional justification (security, necessity); mythopoesis = narrative / historical / mythological justification
legitimation_mode.source: van Leeuwen, T. — Discourse and Practice: New Tools for Critical Discourse Analysis (Oxford UP, 2008)

frame_function.description: Rhetorical function of the frame in the propaganda narrative (Snow & Benford / Entman)
frame_function.notes: diagnostic = defines the problem and attributes blame; prognostic = proposes solution or calls to action; motivational = emotional or moral mobilisation of the audience
frame_function.source: Snow, D. & Benford, R. — Ideology, Frame Resonance and Participant Mobilisation, International Social Movement Research 1 (1988); Entman, R. — Framing: Toward Clarification of a Fractured Paradigm, Journal of Communication 43(4) (1993)

dehumanisation_level.description: Severity on Stanton's 10-stage genocide prevention scale applied to language in the article
dehumanisation_level.notes: 1=Classification (us/them dichotomy); 2=Symbolisation (labelling, badges); 3=Discrimination (legal/social exclusion language); 4=Dehumanisation (animal/disease metaphors); 5=Organisation (calls for organised action against group); 6=Polarisation (no middle ground); 7=Preparation (lists, identity documents, cleansing); 8=Persecution (deprivation of rights); 9=Extermination (mass killing language); 10=Denial (post-atrocity cover-up)
dehumanisation_level.source: Stanton, G. — The Ten Stages of Genocide (Genocide Watch, 1996, updated 2013)

temporality.description: Temporal register of the propaganda narrative (Flood / Mink)
temporality.notes: retrospective = golden age, historical grievance, foundational origin story; contemporaneous = current crisis, present threat requiring action now; prospective = victory narrative, eschatological end-state, promised future
temporality.source: Flood, C. — Political Myth (Routledge, 2002); Mink, L. — History and Fiction as Modes of Comprehension, New Literary History 1(3) (1970)

greimas_actantial.description: Structural narrative grammar assigning actantial roles in the propaganda story (not yet computed per-trope — documented for future use)
greimas_actantial.source: Greimas, A.J. — Sémantique structurale (Larousse, 1966); Propp, V. — Morphology of the Folktale (1928)

rhetorical_tropes.theme: External Threat / Foreign Interference

historical_echoes.context: Plenum of the Central Committee, March 1937 — speech launching the Great Terror
historical_echoes.quote: Wreckers, diversionists, and spies who have been agents of foreign intelligence services have penetrated our Party, Soviet, economic, and military organisations.
historical_echoes.analogy_link: Both frame domestic political opponents as agents of a foreign enemy, making any internal dissent an act of treason rather than legitimate opposition.

historical_echoes.context: Speech in Wheeling, West Virginia, February 9, 1950
historical_echoes.quote: I have here in my hand a list of 205 — a list of names that were made known to the Secretary of State as being members of the Communist Party and who nevertheless are still working and shaping policy in the State Department.
historical_echoes.analogy_link: The claim of a hidden enemy list — unfalsifiable, immune to rebuttal — is structurally identical to accusations of 'foreign agents' infiltrating Ukrainian civil society.

historical_echoes.context: "Communism with the Mask Off" — speech at Nuremberg Rally, 1935. Source: Calvin University German Propaganda Archive, goeb58.htm
historical_echoes.quote: Bolshevism is the declared enemy of all nations and of all religions and of all human civilisation… He has set up a barrier against world Bolshevism against which the waves of this vile Asiatic-Jewish flood break in vain.
historical_echoes.analogy_link: Germany as the lone civilisational bulwark against an ideological foreign infection — the direct structural ancestor of Russian framing as the defender of tradition against a Western-engineered cultural and political invasion.

historical_echoes.context: NKVD Order No. 00447, July 1937 — mass operation against 'anti-Soviet elements'
historical_echoes.quote: Former kulaks, criminals and other anti-Soviet elements who have returned from camps… are to be immediately arrested and, after trial by troikas, shot or sent to camps.
historical_echoes.analogy_link: Bureaucratic dehumanisation of political opponents as 'elements' managed by foreign powers — the same logic used to frame civic protesters as foreign-funded saboteurs.

modern_examples.context: Address to the Federal Assembly, April 21, 2021. Source: en.kremlin.ru/events/president/news/65418
modern_examples.quote: Those who have staged coups and colour revolutions in other countries, those who have tried to knock Russia off this path, are badly mistaken. They organise provocations at our borders and recruit agents of influence to undermine our society from within.
modern_examples.trope_match: foreign_saboteur — the foreign-funded internal enemy framing applied explicitly to Russia's own borders

rhetorical_tropes.theme: The Cult of the Infallible Leader

historical_echoes.context: Quotations from Chairman Mao (Little Red Book), 1964
historical_echoes.quote: The force at the core leading our cause forward is the Chinese Communist Party. The theoretical basis guiding our thinking is Marxism-Leninism.
historical_echoes.analogy_link: Party and leader as the single legitimate source of truth; to question the leader is to question reality itself.

historical_echoes.context: "Look Confidently to the Helmsman!" — Das Reich, March 1945. Source: Calvin University German Propaganda Archive, goeb80.htm
historical_echoes.quote: Look with confidence to the helmsman and with united strength toward the goal! Each German must be sure that it can and will end only with victory and our complete self-assertion. This war is not only a matter of the laurel wreath for our people, but of its entire existence.
historical_echoes.analogy_link: The helmsman metaphor insulates the leader from accountability for military disasters: the ship may be sinking, but the solution is more trust in the captain, never a change of course — identical to the logic of rallying around Putin as Russian forces suffer setbacks.

historical_echoes.context: Sportpalast Total War speech, Berlin, 18 February 1943. Source: Calvin University German Propaganda Archive, goeb36.htm
historical_echoes.quote: Are you ready to follow the Führer as the phalanx of the homeland, standing behind the fighting army? The people want action. It is time for it!
historical_echoes.analogy_link: Manufactured popular consent for total escalation — the leader does not impose the war on the people but appears to respond to their spontaneous demand for it. Used after Stalingrad to frame intensified mobilisation as a popular uprising rather than a state directive.

historical_echoes.figure: Kim Il-sung / Korean Central News Agency
historical_echoes.context: North Korean state media, formative period 1948–1972
historical_echoes.quote: The Great Leader Comrade Kim Il-sung is the sun of the nation and the lodestar of its liberation. He is the father of all Korean people.
historical_echoes.analogy_link: The 'sun' metaphor removes the leader from ordinary political accountability — he illuminates rather than governs, making failure impossible by definition.

modern_examples.context: Annual address to the Federal Assembly, February 29, 2024. Source: en.kremlin.ru/events/president/news/73585
modern_examples.quote: Russia is an open country and a civilisation-state at the same time. Russia has always been and remains a state-civilisation. Our values, our culture, our history, our language — this is what unites us, this is what makes Russia Russia. Those who serve Russia honestly and faithfully are our heroes.
modern_examples.trope_match: paternal_protector — leader as embodiment and guardian of the civilisational state; service to Russia is framed as a sacred vocation

rhetorical_tropes.theme: Traditional Values vs. Modern Degeneracy

historical_echoes.context: Doctrine of Fascism, 1932. English text via Gutenberg Project (pg14058)
historical_echoes.quote: War alone brings all human energies to their highest tension and sets a seal of nobility on peoples who have the courage to face it… The State is an absolute before which individuals and groups are relative. The nation is created by the State, which gives the people an effective existence.
historical_echoes.analogy_link: War as ennobling civilisational test and the state as the only legitimate moral entity — individual suffering becomes politically meaningless, making mass sacrifice not just acceptable but spiritually necessary. This is the operational theology behind 'we do not count casualties' Russian war communication.

historical_echoes.context: Speech to SS Group Leaders, Posen, October 4, 1943
historical_echoes.quote: We had the moral right, we had the duty to our people, to destroy this people which wanted to destroy us.
historical_echoes.analogy_link: The self-defence framing of civilisational violence — extermination recast as moral obligation to preserve a threatened culture.

historical_echoes.context: Ober-Procurator of the Holy Synod, advisor to Tsar Alexander III, 1880s
historical_echoes.quote: Parliamentary government is the great lie of our time… Democracy means the rule of the street, the tyranny of mediocrity, the destruction of all that is sacred.
historical_echoes.analogy_link: The direct ancestor of modern Kremlin anti-Westernism: democracy as moral degeneration, autocracy as spiritual hygiene.

modern_examples.context: Speech at the signing of treaties on the accession of new territories, September 30, 2022. Source: en.kremlin.ru/events/president/news/69465
modern_examples.quote: Do we want to have here, in our country, in Russia, 'parent number one, parent number two and parent number three' instead of 'mum' and 'dad'? Do we want our schools to impose on our children, from their earliest days in school, perversions that lead to degradation and extinction? … This is all unacceptable to us. We have a different future of our own. They are outright satanists.
modern_examples.trope_match: moral_purification — the West explicitly labelled as Satanic, with Russia as the defender of children and natural order against civilisational degeneracy

rhetorical_tropes.theme: Labelling the Enemy as Nazi / Fascist

eco_properties: Enemies Too Strong and Too Weak

historical_echoes.context: "The Jews Are Guilty!" — Das Reich, 16 November 1941. Source: Calvin University German Propaganda Archive, goeb1.htm
historical_echoes.quote: Every Jew is our enemy in this historic struggle, regardless of whether he vegetates in a Polish ghetto or carries on his parasitic existence in Berlin… The Jews are to blame for each German soldier who falls in this war. They have him on their conscience, and they must also pay for it.
historical_echoes.analogy_link: Collective ethnic guilt as propaganda engine: every individual member of the group is held personally responsible for the war, making indiscriminate action against any of them morally justified — structurally identical to 'every Ukrainian is a Nazi' framing that delegitimises all Ukrainian civilian casualties.

historical_echoes.context: "The War and the Jews" — Das Reich, 1943. Source: Calvin University German Propaganda Archive, goeb37.htm
historical_echoes.quote: This war is a war of the Jewish race and its subject people against Western culture… Jewry wanted this war. The instigators are to be found in the foreground.
historical_echoes.analogy_link: The 'they started it' inversion — the aggressor retroactively becomes the victim of an enemy conspiracy that 'wanted' the war. This is the exact structure of Russian claims that NATO/the West/Ukraine 'provoked' and 'wanted' the 2022 war.

historical_echoes.figure: Slobodan Milošević / Serbian state media RTS
historical_echoes.context: Serbian television coverage of the Croatian and Bosnian wars, 1991–1995
historical_echoes.quote: The Ustasha [Croatian] leadership is continuing the genocide of the Serbian people. Our special operation is a defensive response to their fascist aggression.
historical_echoes.analogy_link: The closest modern structural parallel: a Slavic state labels its neighbour as irredeemably fascist and genocidal to justify military invasion — identical framing to Russian 'de-Nazification' of Ukraine.

historical_echoes.context: Soviet reaction to West German rearmament and NATO membership, 1954–1955
historical_echoes.quote: The remilitarisation of West Germany and the creation of a Wehrmacht represents a direct revival of Hitlerite fascism on German soil. The NATO powers are enabling a new Nazi threat to peace-loving peoples.
historical_echoes.analogy_link: The Soviet prototype for post-war 'Nazi' labelling as geopolitical weapon: any Western military development becomes 'fascist', making diplomatic engagement impossible and military vigilance morally mandatory.

historical_echoes.context: Radio address justifying the Soviet invasion of Finland, November 30, 1939
historical_echoes.quote: The Finnish White Guards and their foreign backers have long been preparing an attack on Leningrad. The Soviet Government has been compelled to take measures to protect the security of the Soviet Union.
historical_echoes.analogy_link: The template for all subsequent Russian 'de-Nazification' and 'protection' operations: the victim is recast as aggressor, and invasion as pre-emptive self-defence against an existential fascist threat.

modern_examples.context: Address announcing the special military operation, February 24, 2022. Source: en.kremlin.ru/events/president/news/67843
modern_examples.quote: The purpose of this operation is to protect people who, for eight years now, have been facing humiliation and genocide perpetrated by the Kyiv regime. To this end, we will seek to demilitarise and denazify Ukraine, as well as bring to trial those who perpetrated numerous bloody crimes against civilians.
modern_examples.trope_match: nazi_label — 'denazify' as the operational verb of the invasion; the Nazi label is not rhetorical decoration but the stated legal and military justification

rhetorical_tropes.theme: Territorial Revisionism and the 'One People' Claim

historical_echoes.context: Sportpalast speech, Berlin, September 26, 1938 — on the Sudetenland crisis
historical_echoes.quote: This is the last territorial claim I have to make in Europe, but it is a claim from which I will not retreat and which, God willing, I will make good.
historical_echoes.analogy_link: The 'final demand' structure — each annexation is framed as a limited correction of historical injustice, never an expansionist project, until the next 'historical injustice' is identified.

historical_echoes.context: Speech at Kosovo Polje, June 28, 1989 — 600th anniversary of the Battle of Kosovo
historical_echoes.quote: Serbia has never had only Serbs living in it. Today, more than in the past, members of other peoples and nationalities also live in it. This is not a disadvantage for Serbia. I am truly convinced that it is its advantage.
historical_echoes.analogy_link: The 'brotherly peoples' framing that simultaneously asserts an organic ethnic unity and denies minority political autonomy — used to claim that Kosovo is inalienably Serbian regardless of its population's wishes.

historical_echoes.context: Russian imperial Pan-Slavism, 1860s–1880s — 'All-Russian' ethnic theory
historical_echoes.quote: Great Russians, Little Russians, and White Russians are not three peoples but three branches of the one Russian tribe; the Ukrainian literary language is an artificial political project of the enemies of Russian unity.
historical_echoes.analogy_link: The direct 19th-century ancestor of Putin's 2021 essay 'On the Historical Unity of Russians and Ukrainians' — denying Ukrainian nationhood as an anti-Russian political construct.

historical_echoes.context: Speech to the Italian parliament on irredentism, May 26, 1927
historical_echoes.quote: The Italian people have a mission in the Mediterranean that goes back to Rome. Dalmatia, Nice, Tunis — these are Italian lands that history and blood have claimed for us.
historical_echoes.analogy_link: The 'blood and history' claim as trump card over current borders and populations — the same logic behind Russian claims that Crimea, Donbas, and 'Novorossiya' are primordially Russian.

modern_examples.context: Address to the Nation, February 21, 2022. Source: en.kremlin.ru/events/president/news/67828
modern_examples.quote: Modern Ukraine was entirely created by Russia or, to be more precise, by Bolshevik, Communist Russia. This process started practically right after the 1917 revolution… Lenin and his associates did it in a way that was extremely harsh on Russia – by separating, severing what is historically Russian land.
modern_examples.trope_match: territorial_myth — Ukraine denied historical existence as a state; its territory framed as Russian land temporarily misplaced by Soviet administrative error

modern_examples.context: Essay 'On the Historical Unity of Russians and Ukrainians', July 12, 2021. Source: en.kremlin.ru/events/president/news/66181
modern_examples.quote: Russians and Ukrainians were one people – a single whole. These words are not just my personal view. It was the view of thousands, millions of people on both sides of what is now called the Russian-Ukrainian border.
modern_examples.trope_match: territorial_myth — the 'one people' claim that dissolves Ukrainian nationhood; population opinion is invoked without evidence to assert a unity that overrides political borders

rhetorical_tropes.theme: Delegitimising Democratic Uprisings as Foreign-Backed Coups

historical_echoes.context: Soviet response to the Hungarian Revolution, November 1956
historical_echoes.quote: The counter-revolutionary uprising in Hungary was organised and directed by imperialist reaction — primarily American — with the active participation of the Horthyite fascist emigration and internal enemy elements.
historical_echoes.analogy_link: The structural template: a mass popular uprising is reframed as a foreign-engineered putsch, rendering all subsequent suppression legitimate self-defence rather than imperial violence.

historical_echoes.context: Soviet framing of the Prague Spring, August 21, 1968
historical_echoes.quote: The party and government leaders of the Czechoslovak Socialist Republic have asked the Soviet Union and other allied states for immediate assistance, including armed forces, in their struggle against counter-revolutionary forces.
historical_echoes.analogy_link: The 'invitation' fiction — framing military invasion as a response to a legitimate request, exactly as Russia framed its 2014 Crimea and 2022 Donbas operations.

historical_echoes.context: Proclamation No. 5 of the Military Junta, September 11, 1973
historical_echoes.quote: The Armed Forces and Carabineros of Chile declare that the Marxist government of Allende has been overthrown, inasmuch as its actions were destroying the country's economy and morals, creating fratricidal hatreds, and placing Chile on the path to becoming a satellite of international communism.
historical_echoes.analogy_link: The coup that calls itself a counter-coup: genuine democratic government is retrospectively reframed as the 'real' coup, and military takeover as restoration of order — the mirror logic of 'Maidan was the coup'.

modern_examples.context: Address to the Nation, February 21, 2022. Source: en.kremlin.ru/events/president/news/67828
modern_examples.quote: In February 2014, an armed coup was carried out in Ukraine – we now know it was organised by the United States and its Western allies… After the coup, those who came to power in Kyiv began identifying themselves as the 'new Ukrainian authorities', but they were not elected by the Ukrainian people.
modern_examples.trope_match: maidan_coup — the coup narrative as the entire foundation of Russia's legal case: if Maidan was a coup, the elected government was illegitimate, and its successor agreements (Minsk, Budapest Memorandum) need not be honoured

rhetorical_tropes.theme: Secret Western Bioweapons, Labs, and Hidden Aggression

eco_properties: Enemies Too Strong and Too Weak

historical_echoes.context: Operation DENVER (Operation INFEKTION), 1983–1987 — KGB disinformation campaign

rhetorical_tropes.theme: Denying or Fabricating Evidence of War Crimes

historical_echoes.context: "Churchill's Lie Factory" — Das Reich, 1941. Source: Calvin University German Propaganda Archive, goeb29.htm
historical_echoes.quote: When one lies, one should lie big, and stick to it. They keep up their lies, even at the risk of looking ridiculous… Mr. Churchill, a genuine John Bull, holds to his lies, and in fact repeats them until he himself believes them.
historical_echoes.analogy_link: The enemy's atrocity evidence is itself proof of their propaganda machinery — the bigger the documented crime, the more obviously it is fabricated for psychological warfare. This makes evidence of atrocities self-refuting: the very existence of Bucha photographs becomes proof they are staged.

historical_echoes.context: Soviet denial of the Katyn massacre, 1943–1990
historical_echoes.quote: The Polish officers were shot by German fascists in autumn 1941. The so-called 'Katyn documents' are crude forgeries manufactured by Hitlerite propaganda services and their Polish collaborators.

historical_echoes.context: Gleiwitz incident, August 31, 1939 — staged attack on German radio station

rhetorical_tropes.theme: Denying Sovereignty: The Target State as Western Puppet

historical_echoes.figure: Vidkun Quisling concept / Nazi occupied Norway
historical_echoes.context: Nazi administration of occupied Western Europe, 1940–1944
historical_echoes.quote: The new Norwegian government under National Samling will restore the sovereignty of Norway in cooperation with the German Reich. The old political class that served foreign financial interests has been swept away.

rhetorical_tropes.theme: NATO Expansion as Existential Provocation

eco_properties: Enemies Too Strong and Too Weak

historical_echoes.figure: Soviet World Peace Council / Cominform propaganda
historical_echoes.context: Soviet-sponsored Peace Movement, 1949–1955 — campaign against NATO and West German rearmament

historical_echoes.quote: Germany is surrounded by enemies who have created alliances of encirclement. In this situation, Germany has no choice but to restore its sovereign military equality. We seek peace, but we will not accept strategic encirclement.
historical_echoes.analogy_link: The 'encirclement' argument as justification for violating treaty obligations and expanding military footprint — structurally identical to Russian arguments that NATO enlargement requires 'corrective' military action.

historical_echoes.analogy_link: The aggressor-as-victim and the third party as mere pretext: Germany did not attack Poland — England used Poland to provoke a war it had long planned. rhetorical_tropes.theme: Accusing the Victim of Genocide to Justify Intervention

rhetorical_tropes.theme: Internal Dissent in a Time of National Crisis Is Treason
modern_keywords: this is not the time for politics

historical_echoes.context: US Espionage Act 1917 and Sedition Act 1918 — WWI domestic dissent suppression
historical_echoes.quote: Whoever, when the United States is at war, shall wilfully cause or attempt to cause insubordination, disloyalty, mutiny, or refusal of duty in the military or naval forces of the United States, shall be punished by a fine of not more than $10,000 or imprisonment for not more than twenty years, or both.
historical_echoes.analogy_link: Legal codification of the unity demand: wartime transforms political dissent from a protected right into a criminal act — demonstrating that the unity-demand trope is not exclusively authoritarian but requires active resistance to prevent abuse in democratic contexts also.

historical_echoes.context: Address to Congress, September 20, 2001 — post-9/11 framing
historical_echoes.quote: Either you are with us, or you are with the terrorists.
historical_echoes.analogy_link: The binary unity demand in democratic context: the elimination of neutral positions and the conflation of dissent with enemy alignment — structurally identical to authoritarian unity rhetoric, though without the same enforcement mechanisms.

modern_examples.figure: Isaias Afwerki / Eritrean Ministry of Information
modern_examples.context: Eritrean state media framing of opposition political activity, 2000s–present
modern_examples.quote: Those who collaborate with foreign powers seeking to destabilise Eritrea are traitors to the national cause. There is no room for division when the nation faces existential threats.
modern_examples.trope_match: unity_demand — any political opposition is conflated with foreign destabilisation, making domestic political pluralism structurally equivalent to national treason

rhetorical_tropes.theme: The Regime Must Protect an Ethnic or Religious Group from Persecution

eco_properties: Enemies Too Strong and Too Weak

historical_echoes.context: Memorandum to the British ambassador, August 25, 1939 — two days before the invasion of Poland
historical_echoes.quote: The German minorities in Poland are being subjected to unbearable atrocities. Germany cannot stand by while blood-brothers are physically annihilated. I have therefore decided to solve the Danzig question and the Polish Corridor problem.
historical_echoes.analogy_link: The Volksdeutsche protection template: a claim of ethnic persecution — fabricated, exaggerated, or real but contextually distorted — as a legal-moral warrant for cross-border military intervention. Reproduced structurally in every kin-state protection argument since.

historical_echoes.context: Serbian Academy of Sciences memorandum, 1986 — intellectual foundation for Bosnian war
historical_echoes.quote: The physical, political, legal, and cultural genocide of the Serbian population of Kosovo and Metohija represents the gravest defeat in the liberation struggle that Serbia has waged… The Serbian people in Kosovo are being subjected to systematic genocide.
historical_echoes.analogy_link: Pre-emptive genocide accusation as political mobilisation: claiming that an ethnic group faces extinction justifies any action taken to 'protect' it, while converting the future perpetrator into the present victim — the intellectual structure behind Russian 'genocide of Russian speakers in Donbas'.

modern_examples.context: Address recognising Donetsk and Luhansk People's Republics, February 21, 2022. Source: en.kremlin.ru/events/president/news/67828
modern_examples.quote: People living in Donbas — Russians — have been subjected to genocide for eight years. We cannot stand aside. Russia will protect its people.
modern_examples.trope_match: ethnic_protection — the genocide framing of the Russian-speaking minority serves as the legal and moral trigger for military intervention, converting invasion into humanitarian protection
